description: We are a passionate and multidisciplinary team dedicated to solving complex space challenges using cutting-edge technology. Our team's core expertise spans Data Science, Data Analysis, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Combined with strong capabilities in Web Development and Web Scraping for real-time data ingestion, we aim to build robust, end-to-end, data-driven solutions for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
AstroGuard is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed for long-duration space missions. It transforms complex NASA biomedical data into clear health statuses, alerts, trends, and actionable recommendations.

The system combines an explainable health analytics engine, a FastAPI backend, and an interactive frontend dashboard. Astronauts can monitor blood, immune, radiation, and overall health indicators through visual cards, view their current health status, ask the Health AI assistant questions using voice, receive text or spoken explanations, and send important health summaries to mission doctors.

AstroGuard also supports data-quality indicators, personal-baseline comparisons, cached data, and offline states to remain useful when communication with Earth is limited.
details:
AstroGuard is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform built using official NASA datasets. The system processes Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, immune biomarker, cardiovascular biomarker, and NASA DONKI space-weather data.

The backend is implemented in Python using Pandas and NumPy for data processing, FastAPI for REST APIs, Pydantic for validated response schemas, and SQLite for offline storage. The pipeline converts the NASA CSV and JSON files into a canonical structure, applies data-quality flags, calculates personal preflight baselines, compares measurements with source-provided reference ranges, detects trends and anomalies, and generates explainable domain and overall health scores.

The system covers immune, metabolic, and cardiovascular health. Hematology is included as a subdomain of immune. Radiation data are presented separately as space-weather context and are not treated as measured crew exposure or included in the personal health score.

AstroGuard returns four clear statuses: NORMAL, WATCH, ACTION_REQUIRED, and DATA_UNAVAILABLE. Every result includes evidence, source traceability, confidence, data-quality information, alerts, and bounded recommendations. Suspicious or missing values remain visible and are never silently corrected or imputed.

A FastAPI layer provides dashboard, timeline, domain, alert, data-quality, radiation, and offline-bundle endpoints for the frontend. A Gemini-powered assistant provides a conversational interface over validated AstroGuard results. It answers questions using structured API-grounded context, preserves the original scores and evidence, supports safety escalation, and prevents unsupported diagnosis or medication advice. Voice interaction uses a microphone or client transcript, while browser speech synthesis can read the validated response aloud.

The frontend is built separately using web technologies and communicates with the backend through JSON and multipart voice endpoints. The system is designed to continue providing cached health results and local fallback responses when Gemini or Earth communication is unavailable.
